title: but pr new --single: publish ONLY the named branch (no ancestor pushes/reviews, no native stack registration) — the agent/automation PR path
description:
OUR FORK'S FEATURE #1 (from fabro-75fb, relocated here as the tracker of record; user directive 2026-10-03: fork + build ourselves, 'genau so wie mit seeds und mulch').

PROBLEM (verified in fabro, PR #369/#370/#372 incident): `but pr new` on a stacked branch pushes the branch AND its ancestors and creates reviews bottom-up — collateral ancestor PRs appear (e.g. line-branch -> frozen-base PRs, the hazard class our gates exist for). Additionally GitButler registers NATIVE GitHub stack metadata on its PRs; on GitHub instances without the async stacked-merge endpoint this BLOCKS every merge path (sync merge refused 'part of a stack', async REST 404s).

CODE SURFACE (located): crates/but/src/command/legacy/forge/review.rs — (a) but_api::legacy::workspace::workspace_branch_and_ancestors_push_only (line ~658) = the ancestor push+review walk; (b) sync_review_stack_after_review_creation (line ~719) = native stack registration; (c) ~line 322 'stacked publication try to recreate a dependency review' = dependency-review recreation. No configuration surface exists (feature flags: only unapply-v3-pgm + single-branch; neither touches PR creation) — verified 2026-10-03.

FEATURE: `--single` flag on `but pr new` (plus a persistent default, e.g. `but config feature pr-single enable`):
- publish ONLY the named branch: no ancestor pushes, no ancestor reviews, no dependency-review recreation;
- skip native stack metadata registration for that review entirely (plain branch PR);
- stacking stays the DEFAULT behavior for interactive use — single is the agent/automation path.

ACCEPTANCE: a stacked two-lane workspace (line + feature lane above) where `but pr new <feature> --single` creates EXACTLY ONE PR (for the feature branch, against its true base), pushes no other refs, registers no stack metadata, and the PR merges through the normal sync path. Tests: CLI flag parsing + the workspace publication path (the review.rs flow) with a fixture workspace; exit unchanged for default invocations.

evidence.tests: but-workspace/but-settings/but-api: 772/772 pass; but: 1936/1941 (5 fails = pre-existing WSL drvfs EACCES artifact, 1 proven on clean master); new: PushScope::BranchOnly behavioral push tests, chain short-circuit on stacked fixture, --single parse, pr-single config round-trip via real binary, prSingle settings serde+persist

closeReason: Implemented and landed via PR #1 (merge b2267789b4): --single publishes exactly one review, pushes no ancestor refs, skips stack registration; pr-single persistent default. Tests green (evidence in extensions).

title: fork release pipeline: v* tag -> but CLI binaries + SHASUMS -> GitHub Release (consumer mise pins switch to fork artifacts)
description:
OUR FORK'S DELIVERY PIPELINE (companion to the --single feature seed; mirrors denkhaus/seeds release conventions — seeds-6475/e160 pattern).

GOAL: ship our own `but` builds so every repo can pin OUR fork (the rollout gate: no repo joins GitButler until this exists).

DESIGN: GitHub Actions on this fork — v* tag -> build the but CLI (cargo build --release -p but) -> linux x86_64 artifact (+ aarch64 if cheap) + SHASUMS.txt -> GitHub Release. Keep tracking upstream main (remote 'upstream' is wired); merges deliberate, like petri/pebble forks in fabro.

CONSUMER SIDE (after first release): switch the mise http:but pins (fabro/.mise.toml, seeds, mulch + global ~/.config/mise/config.toml) from releases.gitbutler.com URLs to our fork's release artifact URLs; version scheme: start fork-local (e.g. 0.22.3-fork.1) so upstream-version collisions stay impossible.

ACCEPTANCE: tag -> release workflow green -> artifact downloadable + checksum-clean -> `mise install http:but` against the new URL resolves and `but --version` reports the fork version in a fresh shell.

evidence.note: workflow green run + artifact download/checksum verification pending the first tag

title: fork-release: stamp CHANNEL=release so the fork binary uses the standard com.gitbutler.app app-data path
description: Found by the coordinator after v0.22.3-fork.1: our fork-release.yaml build job does not set CHANNEL, so crates/but/build.rs defaults IDENTIFIER to com.gitbutler.app.dev. The released fork binary therefore looks for its project registry and app data under ~/.local/share/com.gitbutler.app.dev instead of the standard com.gitbutler.app path that every upstream but install and the GUI use (crates/but/src/lib.rs:307, crates/but-path/src/lib.rs AppChannel::new). The coordinator bridged locally with a symlink. FIX: set CHANNEL=release in the build job env of .github/workflows/fork-release.yaml (build.rs maps release -> com.gitbutler.app). Takes effect from the next tag (v0.22.3-fork.2 onward); v0.22.3-fork.1 binaries keep the dev identity.

title: fork: keep the git index in sync with the workspace (stale index makes git diff/status lie)
description:
FORK REQUEST 1 — keep the classic git index in sync with the workspace commit (or a `but sync-index`)

OBSERVED (fabro multi-agent session, 2026-10-03): `but` does not maintain the classic git index. After `but commit`/branch operations the index holds a stale tree, so `git status` shows phantom `MM` entries and `git diff` reports changes that do not exist (worktree == HEAD, verified via blob hashes: index 09e0aaf316 vs HEAD/worktree bd6157ec74). Every git-diff-based tool (evidence scripts, review flows, gates, agents) then lies; we had to run `git reset` (mixed) manually, and every NEW agent session hits this again.

DEMAND (either is fine): (a) after workspace-affecting operations, refresh the index to match the workspace commit; or (b) add `but sync-index` (plus a `but doctor` hint) that detects index != workspace-tree and offers the repair. (a) is preferable — zero ceremony.

RISK: unknown if GB relies on index staleness anywhere; if so, (b) is the safe variant.

--- STATUS (2026-10-03, implemented on the fork) ---
REPRODUCED: after `but commit <file>:<hunk>` the on-disk index holds the merge result, which still
contains the uncommitted worktree content. `git status --porcelain` then reports `MM <path>`
(staged plus unstaged) and `git diff` shows nothing, so every diff-based tool believes there is
nothing to commit. Seen in a scratch repo created by `but setup`, and in the low-level harness
(crates/but-core/tests/core/worktree/checkout.rs).
CAUSE: crates/but-core/src/worktree/checkout/function.rs - `checkout_index` writes
`checkout_target`, an index built from the 3-way merge result that preserves uncommitted content, to
`.git/index`; and that write lived inside the `old_tree != new_tree` branch, which committing a hunk
never enters because the workspace tree does not change.
FIX: `checkout_index` no longer writes `.git/index` (`update_index(false)`). Afterwards the index is
brought in line for exactly two path sets, and nothing else is touched:
- the paths this operation changed in the head tree (previous HEAD tree vs checked out tree): the
  index takes the checked out entry, or drops the entry if the path is gone from it. This is the fix
  for committing a hunk, which never changes the workspace tree;
- the paths the checkout rewrote in the worktree (worktree snapshot vs merge result): the index
  follows what was checked out, so moved-away content leaves no phantom entry behind.
Unresolved conflicts keep their stages 1/2/3, written explicitly now that libgit2 no longer does it.
Every other index entry is state Git was left in - staged changes, renames, `git rm --cached` - and
survives untouched, which is what `worktree_and_index_deletions_are_ignored_in_snapshots` pins down.
Consequence, deliberate: for a path the operation consumed, the index now holds the committed content
instead of the worktree content, so Git reports the leftover hunks as unstaged. Two expectations in
`worktree_snapshot_reapplies_with_hunk_granularity` were updated for that (`832f532` -> `4afd67b` and
`M  file` -> ` M file`), with its comment rewritten. Earlier attempt "index := checked out tree
wholesale" broke those tests and was discarded: the index is not stateless, unrelated staged state has
to survive.
TESTS: `checkout_puts_the_checked_out_tree_into_the_index` (but-core; red without the fix, and it
covers the "workspace tree unchanged" case) plus the CLI-level
`committing_one_hunk_keeps_the_remaining_worktree_change_unstaged` (crates/but).
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: a `but sync-index` command plus doctor hint - the cause is fixed, so no repair
surface is needed. Remaining gap known but out of scope: operations that materialize without a
checkout (e.g. `but uncommit`) never run this sync.


--- SPEC-REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (2026-10-03, same session) ---
The spec review found two gaps that are now closed:
1. The `merge_base_override` path wrote the index wholesale (`git2_repo.apply(.., ApplyLocation::Index, ..)` with an
   `index.read_tree(tree)` fallback), which dropped staged state and `git rm --cached` entries - exactly the effect
   this seed rejected elsewhere. That write is gone; the scoped sync at the end of the checkout is now the only
   index writer in this function.
2. "Operations that materialize without a checkout do not sync" is fixed: `but_rebase`'s `materialize()` now calls
   `but_core::worktree::sync_index_with_tree` for the paths where the head tree moved when it materializes without a
   checkout (e.g. `but uncommit`). Verified A/B with a scratch repo: without the sync, `but uncommit` leaves
   `git status --porcelain` at `M  f` (staged) with an EMPTY `git diff` and the worktree content in the index;
   with it, ` M f` plus the uncommitted change visible to `git diff`. Guarded by the CLI test
   `uncommit_leaves_the_on_disk_index_describing_head` (red without the sync, green with it).
`but sync-index` remains deliberately unbuilt: both causes are fixed at the source.

LANDED on the fork: commit d24ef86dab (branch master, pushed to origin/master). Review: two-axis code review performed; findings folded in.

title: fork: ergonomic hunk-level commits for shared files (multi-agent, one checkout)
description:
FORK REQUEST 2 — ergonomic hunk-level commits for shared files (multi-agent, one checkout)

OBSERVED (2026-10-03, two agents in one fabro checkout): the repo's shared tracker file (.seeds/issues.jsonl, append-only JSONL) is written by BOTH agents. `but commit <file-id>` commits the whole file, so agent A's commit swept agent B's in-flight rows (claims landed in an unrelated commit; both agents then had to coordinate manually over agent messaging). Hunk IDs exist (`but diff` shows them) but selecting exactly one's own lines is fiddly and error-prone under concurrency.

DEMAND: make per-line/per-hunk commit ergonomic and non-interactive, e.g. `but commit --file <path> --hunks` that LISTS stable hunk IDs with a preview, and `but commit <hunk-ids>` that commits exactly those. Bonus: a `--dry-run` showing the resulting commit content. This is THE core primitive for N agents sharing one checkout with shared append-only files.

--- STATUS (2026-10-03, fork work started) ---
Per-hunk commits ALREADY work in this fork: `but commit <file-id>:<hunk-id>` is wired end to end
(crates/but/src/command/legacy/commit.rs -> UncommittedSelection -> Transaction::create_commit) and
`but diff --json` lists the hunk ids. What this seed adds is ergonomics:
- `--file <PATH>`: path-anchored selector instead of a positional id.
- `--hunks`: list the file's hunk ids (with the existing diff rendering) without committing.
- `--dry-run`: DEFERRED (user decision 2026-10-03, nice-to-have). It needs `DryRun` plumbed through
  SingleBranchMode::transaction_with_workspace_setup (hardcodes DryRun::No) AND the transaction
  returns a commit id plus workspace state despite the rollback, so the output would claim a commit
  that does not exist.

KNOWN LIMITATION, tracked separately: hunk ids are snapshot-scoped, not durable handles. The hunk
part is a content hash whose minimum length derives from neighbouring hunks
(crates/but/src/id/mod.rs) and the file part lengthens as commits/branches appear, so two agents on
one append-only file cannot rely on an id captured earlier.

LANDED on the fork: commit 1f23a149a0 (branch master, pushed to origin/master). Review: two-axis code review performed; findings folded in.

title: fork: `but sha <branch>` — pushable SHA for release tooling (workspace commit is never pushed)
description:
FORK REQUEST 3 — expose a pushable SHA for tooling (`but sha <branch>`)

OBSERVED (fabro release flow, 2026-10-03): release scripts derive tags via `git rev-parse --short HEAD` — under GitButler that yields the LOCAL workspace commit, which is never pushed. Our image tag 0.362.0-fork.3-8f0874d91 therefore references a commit that cannot be resolved on origin (tree identical to the pushed line commit, but not the same object).

DEMAND: `but sha <branch>` printing the branch's real tip commit (the one `but push` publishes), so tooling tags a pushable sha. Alternative: an opt-in that publishes workspace commits. The command variant is enough for us.

--- STATUS (2026-10-03, implemented on the fork) ---
`but sha <branch>` prints the commit `but push` publishes for that branch. Resolution reuses the push
loop's own step: `but_workspace::legacy::push::pushable_segment_tip()` (graph.tip_skip_empty) and
`pushable_branch_tip()` (the branch's own segment). The push loop now calls the same helper, so the
printed SHA cannot drift from what a push sends. Prints the full SHA on its own; exits non-zero when
the branch names no segment of the workspace.
TEST: `sha_prints_the_commit_a_push_publishes` (crates/but/tests/but/command/sha.rs) pushes the branch
to a bare remote and asserts the SHA printed before the push is the one on origin after it.
DOCS: crates/but/skill/references/reference.md (Remote Operations) and the Git-to-But map in SKILL.md.


LANDED on the fork: commit 951efd0758 (branch master, pushed to origin/master). Review: two-axis code review performed; findings folded in.

title: fork: stable hunk handles for concurrent agents (uncommitted hunk ids are snapshot-scoped)
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-03, while implementing gitbutler-3e3d): hunk ids shown by `but diff` are not durable handles. The hunk part is a content hash with a minimum prefix length derived from neighbouring hunks (crates/but/src/id/mod.rs, min 3 chars for detected agents, collision disambiguation appends `#i-n`), and the file part is a reverse-hex path id that can lengthen as commits or branches appear.

CONSEQUENCE: two agents editing one shared append-only file in one checkout cannot capture a hunk id and rely on it a moment later; the id may have moved or lengthened. Per-hunk commits therefore work, but the handle to select them is racy under concurrency.

DEMAND: a stable way to address exactly the hunks a caller just saw, e.g. an explicit "commit these diff lines/hunks that I am passing now" input (patch text), or ids that do not change while the file's hunk set changes. Decide the shape with upstream before building; the seed exists to keep the gap visible (see gitbutler-3e3d).

RESOLUTION (2026-10-04): option A built — `but commit --patch <FILE|->` (commit dfbfcda29b). A unified diff as `git diff` writes it selects exactly its hunks: byte-exact content match against the file's current uncommitted hunks (context included, `@@` and no-newline markers stripped as comparison basis), positions may shift, selection carries the CURRENT hunk positions. No match / ambiguous duplicate bodies → hard error with re-diff hint. `--patch --hunks` previews the matched hunks with current IDs. Rejected: length-stable full hashes (does not fix collision/dangling races), snapshot-validated positional handles (makes the race explicit instead of removing it; retry loops instead of throughflow). Upstream issue drafted the same day (shape families + recommendation) for upstream alignment.

LANDED on the fork: commit dfbfcda29b (branch master). Tests: 7 patch_selection unit tests (parse git-style/bare/rename/no-newline/repeated files; match by content not position; stale and ambiguous rejected); but lib suite 995/995; clippy clean; live smoke in a shared GB workspace: preview matched, stale patch refused with hint.

UPSTREAM (2026-10-04): issue filed — https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/issues/16224

title: fork: `but pr new` cannot set the review BASE — reviews always target the repo target branch
description:
OBSERVED 2026-10-03 (fabro multi-agent session, fork workflow): `but pr new b869-provider-scoped-gate --single` created exactly ONE review for the branch — `--single` itself works as documented (no ancestor/collateral reviews, no native stack registration). The problem is the review BASE: the review was opened against the GitButler TARGET branch. In our fork the GB target is deliberately `origin/main` (the frozen upstream base) while every line PR must base on our applied line branch `denkhaus`, so:
- the review never ran the base-scoped CI (our dogfood-gate triggers on pull_request[branches: denkhaus]), and
- merging it would have landed the change on the frozen base — an ADR violation.

Why the target cannot simply be switched: `but config target` is repo-wide, and setting it to our line branch is refused because a target cannot be the branch that is applied/work-in-progress (denkhaus is the applied line branch). The GitButler app has per-branch targets, the CLI exposes none.
Workaround we used: close the GB-created review and recreate it with `gh pr create --base denkhaus` (and `gh pr edit --base` is not an option — the GraphQL UpdatePullRequest is refused for this token). Net effect: `but pr new` is unusable for our PR workflow, so we `but push <lane>` and open reviews with gh — losing the native stack metadata the CLI is supposed to maintain.

DEMAND: a per-invocation review base, e.g. `but pr new --base <branch>`, and/or a CLI-exposed per-branch target (the app already models it). `--single` should keep meaning 'one review, no ancestors'; the base should be independent of it.

EVIDENCE: denkhaus/fabro PR #382 (GB-created, base main, closed as superseded) vs PR #383 (recreated with gh, base denkhaus).

RESOLUTION (2026-10-04): delivered as `but pr new --base <BRANCH>` (commit 939528fe53) for single-branch publication. The demand "base independent of --single" is REJECTED for stacked publication: the stacked post-creation sync (`sync_review_stack_after_review_creation`) derives review bases from the workspace stack by design and recomputes them (`compute_review_target_updates`), so a custom base would be overridden immediately. A stacked custom base would need a sync-level carve-out; reopen with that scope if a real case appears. The fork flow (`--single` per the parallel-agent contract) is fully covered. Accepted inputs: plain branch names, `refs/heads/<b>`, `refs/remotes/<remote>/<b>`; own-branch bases rejected.

LANDED on the fork: commit 939528fe53 (branch master, pushed to origin/master). Tests: review_base_override unit tests; forge::review suite 33/33; clippy clean.

title: fork: but commit silently places at the stack tip — fail closed (or infer ownership) when several lanes are applied
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-04, fabro sprint 14): with several lanes stacked in one workspace (line branch 'denkhaus' applied + a sibling lane above it), `but commit <files>` placed the commit at the TIP OF THE STACK — the sibling's lane — not on the lane the operator was working on. Repair needed `but move <id> --branch <line>`. The help text documents the behavior ("the commit is placed at the tip of that stack"), but for the multi-agent experiment this is a silent-misplacement hazard: an agent committing to ITS lane while another lane sits above lands work in the sibling's PR.

DESIGN OPTIONS (decision needed):
(a) ownership inference: when the selected changes overlap files/lanes, default to the lane OWNING the majority of the selected changes (heuristic, may surprise);
(b) fail closed with a teaching error when more than one lane is applied and no explicit --branch/--above/--below was passed ("N lanes applied; pass --branch <name>") — consistent with the fork's fail-closed posture for agent operation;
(c) status quo + docs.

RECOMMENDATION: (b) — silent cross-lane placement is the worst outcome for concurrent agents; one explicit flag is cheap; single-lane workspaces keep the current zero-flag flow.

ACCEPTANCE: in a workspace with two applied lanes, `but commit <files>` without targeting flags either refuses with the teaching error or lands on the lane owning the changes; it never silently lands on a lane whose name was never mentioned in the invocation.

EVIDENCE: fabro sprint-14 ledger note; repaired via `but move ozuo --branch denkhaus` (commit 8ea5b98fd was created on b869-provider-scoped-gate, moved to denkhaus).

RESOLUTION (2026-10-04): option (b) built, scoped to NAMED selections (commit 21e9a21cdd). `but commit <changes>`, `--file` and `--patch` selections (and `but pick`'s named selection) fail closed in a multi-lane stack: "N lanes are applied (a, b); a bare commit would land on the topmost" + hint for --branch/--above/--below. Bare commits (everything uncommitted) and interactive TUI picks keep the tip default — the flow right after `but branch new` relies on it, and a selection-less commit names nothing to protect (the seed's DEMAND text covered `but commit <files>` only). Upstream check 2026-10-04: no issue/PR in flight on lane-default placement (searched "commit lane", "commit tip stack", "but commit"); no upstream issue filed for this one yet — fork-local posture first.

LANDED on the fork: commit 21e9a21cdd (branch master). Tests: bare_commit_fails_closed_when_several_lanes_are_applied + bare_commit_without_a_named_selection_keeps_the_tip_default (integration); suite 961 passed with only 5 pre-existing environmental failures (verified identical on clean master); clippy clean.

title: fork: `but branch update` fails on a lane LEVEL with its remote ('Integration steps cannot be empty') and cannot repair a worktree left behind by a plain-git fast-forward
description:
OBSERVED (2026-10-04, fabro line, fork v0.22.3-fork.5): after a run PR merged into the tracked remote branch, `but branch update denkhaus` failed with

  Error: Integration steps cannot be empty

while `but status` already displayed the remote merge commit in the lane (marker "(upstream: on origin/denkhaus)"). The WORKTREE was NOT refreshed: a file the merge added (.fabro/scripts/toolchain-guard.sh) was absent on disk, so the branch looked integrated but its content was not materialized. After two local commits landed on the lane, the very same command printed "Updated branch denkhaus." and the merged file appeared. The same error also appears when the lane is exactly LEVEL with its remote (no divergence at all), where it is harmless but confusing.

Likely shape: the planner produces no steps for a pure fast-forward (lane strictly behind, no local-only commits) and reports the empty plan as an error instead of integrating, leaving the worktree stale.

DEMAND:
(a) a lane strictly behind its remote integrates (fast-forward) and the worktree carries the remote's content afterwards;
(b) a lane level with its remote reports a clear no-op (e.g. "denkhaus is already up to date with origin/denkhaus"), not an integration error;
(c) when the integration genuinely cannot proceed (conflicts, detached state, ...) the message names the observed state and the next action, instead of "Integration steps cannot be empty";
(d) "updated" must never be reported (in status or otherwise) while the worktree still reflects the pre-merge content.

ACCEPTANCE: with a local lane strictly behind origin/<lane> and no local commits, `but branch update <lane>` fast-forwards and the worktree contains the remote's files; running it twice in a row is a clean no-op; a blocked integration names why.

EVIDENCE: fabro session 2026-10-04, PR #385 merge (45f890d34) — error + missing file + retry success after local commits; the level-lane variant reproduced at the same session's start.

WORKAROUND used: commit local work first, then retry `but branch update <lane>` (the retry succeeds), or verify a merged file exists on disk before trusting the lane display.

REPRODUCED TWICE in one session (2026-10-04, fabro line): (1) after PR #385 merged (worktree missing .fabro/scripts/toolchain-guard.sh, lane display already showed the merge) — two local commits, retry, then "Updated branch denkhaus." and the file appeared; (2) after PR #386 merged (journal-only) — same error, same fix (commit the pending tracker change, retry twice, then the merged file appeared). The retry-after-commit workaround is reliable but must be discovered by hand each time.

--- RE-DIAGNOSED (2026-10-05, scripted CLI repro, fork 1722423e10) ---

Evidence: /home/denkhaus/.local/share/but-fork-evidence/cd55/report.md, rerunnable with
`python3 /home/denkhaus/.local/share/but-fork-evidence/cd55/run_demo.py` (one throwaway repo per
scenario, local bare `origin`, no token/GUI).

CORRECTION to this seed's framing: the literal combination "lane strictly behind AND the
`(upstream: ...)` marker AND the empty-step error" could NOT be reproduced - the two observations
were made at two moments of the same session. What actually happens, per state:

- S1 lane strictly behind (plain commit), lane ref stale: `but branch update` SUCCEEDS
  ("Updated branch denkhaus."), the lane ref reaches the remote tip and the remote's new file
  appears on disk. Demand (a) is already satisfied today.
- S2 lane exactly LEVEL with its remote (and any second run right after a successful update):
  `Error: Integration steps cannot be empty`, exit 1, nothing changes.
- S3 lane ref ALREADY at the remote tip while `gitbutler/workspace` (HEAD) is older - e.g. after a
  plain `git fetch origin <lane>:<lane>`: the file exists in the ref, is ABSENT on disk, and
  `but branch update` fails with the same empty-step error, so nothing repairs it. Committing is
  impossible in this state (`but commit` -> "Head stack has no ref"; `but commit -b <lane>` ->
  "A branch named '<lane>' exists but is not applied"), so the workaround recorded above does NOT
  apply to it.
- S4 behind + one local-only commit: SUCCEEDS (the workaround shape).
- S6 remote advanced by a forge MERGE commit: `but branch update` reports SUCCESS
  ("Updated branch denkhaus.") yet the rebuilt lane commit is an EMPTY copy of the merge commit,
  the merged content never reaches the tree, `but status` keeps listing the merge's second-parent
  commit as upstream-only, and repeated runs stack further empty copies without converging.

MECHANISM (measured): the pull-rebase plan is `pick <each upstream commit>` chained with the
non-integrated local commits; both empty <=> no divergence the planner can act on.
`integrate_branch_with_steps` then bails at
crates/but-workspace/src/branch/integrate_branch_upstream/mod.rs:124, reached from
crates/but/src/command/branch/update.rs.

SPLIT: the level/no-op case (S2) and the stale-worktree case (S3) are this seed; the merge-commit
non-convergence (S6) is a separate planner defect, filed as gitbutler-2825.

title: fork: no non-interactive way to commit part of a hunk — a neighbour's adjacent append fuses the rows (sub-hunk selection)
description:
NO NON-INTERACTIVE WAY TO SELECT PART OF A HUNK (sub-hunk selection).

OBSERVED (2026-10-05, scripted reproduction with the fork binary `crates/but` build of 2a8bde2b7b; raw evidence in /home/denkhaus/.local/share/but-fork-evidence/hunk-race/report.md, rerunnable with `BE=/home/denkhaus/dev/gitbutler/target/debug/but python3 /home/denkhaus/.local/share/but-fork-evidence/hunk-race/run_demo.py`, case 2).

Workload: two agents write ONE append-only JSONL tracker (`.seeds/issues.jsonl`, one object per line) in ONE checkout. A appends a row -> `but diff` shows `qwx:142`. B appends a row directly below.

Adjacent additions are ONE hunk, so:
- A's ID is gone (`Error: Could not find uncommitted change: 'qwx:142'`), the fused hunk prints as `qwx:68f`;
- committing by the re-read ID puts BOTH rows into A's commit (git show confirms seq 21 AND the neighbour's seq 22).

ALREADY TRIED (commit dfbfcda29b): `but commit --patch` matches a patch hunk BYTE-EXACTLY against a current hunk BODY. A hand-trimmed patch containing only A's row fails hard:

  Error: cannot commit patch hunks of log.jsonl: a hunk of the patch is not among the file's
  current changes; the file changed since the patch was captured
  hint: re-run `but diff <file>` and rebuild the patch

=> after fusion there is NO non-interactive selector that names A's row alone. Today's options are: commit the neighbour's row too, stop and ask a human, or `but commit --interactive` (TTY-only, unusable for agents).

CONSEQUENCE: the primitive this multi-agent workflow needs - "commit exactly the lines I added, or fail" - is unavailable whenever another writer appends near our change. This is the case the ID system cannot solve at ALL, because it is a granularity question, not an identity question: three-character prefixes, the `#i-n` collision index, and `--patch` content matching all operate on whole hunks.

DEMAND: a non-interactive selection that can address a SUB-RANGE of a current hunk by content. Candidate shape (propose before building): extend the `--patch` matcher so a patch hunk may match a CONTIGUOUS WINDOW inside a current hunk - the patch's old-side lines (context + removals) must appear contiguously in the file's current old side, and the selection is that window's new-side lines. Fail closed on no match and on several indistinguishable matches, exactly as today.

ACCEPTANCE: two writers, adjacent appends, one fused hunk -> A's patch (its row + context) commits A's row only and B's row stays uncommitted; a patch matching no contiguous window errors with the existing re-diff hint; byte-identical twins stay a hard error pointing at `but diff` IDs.

RELATED: upstream issue https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/issues/16224 , our comment 5993596417 asks upstream whether they want the cheap whole-hunk version now or would rather wait for sub-hunk selection; the answer decides whether this is fork-only or an upstream PR. See also gitbutler-6e86 (stable hunk handles) and gitbutler-3e3d (ergonomic hunk-level commits).

title: fork: `but branch update` reports success but never integrates a lane whose remote advanced by a MERGE commit (empty copies, no convergence)
description:
A LANE WHOSE REMOTE ADVANCED BY A MERGE COMMIT NEVER CONVERGES, AND THE COMMAND CLAIMS SUCCESS.

OBSERVED (2026-10-05, scripted CLI repro, fork 1722423e10; evidence
/home/denkhaus/.local/share/but-fork-evidence/cd55/report.md, scenario S6, rerunnable with
`python3 /home/denkhaus/.local/share/but-fork-evidence/cd55/run_demo.py`).

The remote of a lane advanced by a forge-style MERGE commit (the shape a "Create a merge commit" PR
produces). Then:

- `but branch update denkhaus` prints `Updated branch denkhaus.` and exits 0;
- the merged file - the content the merge brings in relative to the lane's old tip - is ABSENT on
  disk and absent from the rebuilt lane commit (`git show` exits 128);
- the rebuilt lane commit is an EMPTY copy of the merge commit: relative to its first parent a merge
  carries no change of its own, so picking it adds nothing;
- `but status` keeps listing the merge's second-parent commit under `(upstream: on origin/<lane>)`;
- repeated runs do not converge: after several runs `refs/heads/<lane>` is still not
  `refs/remotes/origin/<lane>`, and every run stacks another empty copy.

CONSEQUENCE: unlike the empty-step error in gitbutler-cd55 (which fails closed), this failure is
silent and wrong: the command reports success, the user reads "Updated branch", and the content of
the merged PR is missing from the worktree. It also breaks cd55's demand (d).

DEMAND: integrating a lane whose upstream advanced by a merge commit brings the merge's CONTENT into
the worktree (what `git merge`/`git pull` would do), or fails closed naming the observed state.
Repeated runs must converge - the second run must be a clean no-op.

ACCEPTANCE: with a lane strictly behind a remote whose tip is a merge commit, one
`but branch update <lane>` puts the merged file on disk and in the lane's tree; a second run is a
no-op; if the merge genuinely cannot be integrated, the message names why and no content is silently
missing.

RELATED: gitbutler-cd55 (same session and script; level/no-op + stale worktree).
